purpose: Update the source-checked literature map after the center-density hostile audit, import compatible theorem interfaces, and determine whether any result changes a first open edge.

weil.first_open_edge: zeta-specific adjacent-support propagation beyond the certified local endpoints

secondary_open_edges: sharp four-cycle endpoint, not a direct strip gate

search_lanes: Weil criteria, explicit formulas, de Branges and canonical systems, local-to-global positivity
Dirichlet-polynomial moments and large values, zero density, primes and shifted convolutions
coefficient-sensitive convex return, nonharmonic Fourier inequalities, discrepancy and inverse theorems
recent primary preprints cited by or subsequent to the 2026-08-29 import
source_policy: Use primary papers, author manuscripts, journal articles, and official preprints. Secondary sources may locate a paper but cannot support an imported theorem statement.
fast_falsifiers: exponent or reconstruction loss exceeding the available margin

decision_rule.priority_change: Only a theorem that improves or removes a first open edge, or gives a new falsifiable sublemma with a complete adapter, changes priority.
decision_rule.supporting_import: A compatible module that leaves a named new edge is recorded as supporting literature, not a solution.
decision_rule.nonapplication: A sign, mask, source, band, resolution, or quantifier mismatch is displayed explicitly.
decision_rule.novelty: No project result is called literature-novel without a targeted search and a statement-level comparison.

hard_stops: Do not merge the Weil and QP/Turan support ledgers.
Do not infer RH from the contemplated narrow strip.
Do not treat a pseudo-node obstruction as an actual-prime refutation.
Do not treat a finite computation or abstract reformulation as an imported asymptotic theorem.
Do not silently replace signed adaptive coefficients by positive or fixed coefficients.
